title: #answer to @brady :)  truly one of the most depressing shows I’ve see...
transcript: I did go see days of wine and roses, which is a new Adam Ghetto musical currently playing at the Atlantic Theatre Company until July 16th. Days of wine and roses is based off the film of the same name, and it follows this couple in the relationship to each other as well as to alcohol. Thus, the wine and roses, I presume, stars Brian Darcy James and Kelly o'hara, both of whom I adore. And I also really love the scores to Floyd Collins and lighten the Piazza. So, naturally, I had to go see this. Overall, I think this is a very well constructed show. There's not a lot that I would change about it. But the entire time, I kept thinking to myself, why did they make this into a musical? It was just really depressing, like, the entire time. And I don't know if, ultimately, the payoff, to me, was worth it. Comparing it to something like Wet Brain that is also about alcoholism and playing off Broadway currently, that, to me, has a really good catharsis that makes me, like, keep thinking about the show. And this just kind of ends, and it's like, why? Why. Why are we telling this story? I don't know. It just. It didn't speak to me personally, but I feel like if somebody is going to get something out of this musical, that it is overall a good musical. Of course, the cast is fantastic. I mean, there is A scene of Kelly o'hara just vacuuming, that is worth the price of admission alone. I will say the style of this musical is a very talk singing. It's not quite operatic. It's more in the style of what Android Webber does a lot, or the composers that diddly MS. And Miss Saigon, where it's not really melodic in nature. It's more like I were having a conversation and it's all in song. And I personally prefer that to like a full blown opera, but that's my personal taste. It's going to drive some people nuts. And this definitely is probably not a show that I would go back and listen to the cast recording of, with the exception of a few songs. Overall, again, I think this is a well constructed musical. It just didn't speak to me personally. Do I think this would transfer to Broadway? I don't know. I don't think so. I don't think that this is a show that they can sell commercially. Maybe we would see a limited run, but I just keep asking myself why? Why? I don't know who they would sell this to. I don't know why it exists. I don't know who else would perform it in the future. I do hope, like I hope with every show that we get a cast recording of it, especially with this cast, cause that deserves to be preserved for sure. But I don't know if this is a show that we're gonna See after this production. So if you wanna see it, I definitely would recommend seeing it before July 16th.
